pages.text: "I only want fish!" Pongi picked just the fish from her plate. Fish, bread, and peas sat in a circle on the plate. Mom, wearing her headscarf, said, "You need to eat bread and peas too."
"I don't like bread! I don't like peas either!" Pongi pushed them to the edge of the plate. Two empty spaces appeared. "I'm strong even if I only eat fish!" Mom quietly looked at the empty spaces.
It was morning. The first boat went past the window with a toot. Pongi plopped down in the doorway. Her legs felt heavy, and she couldn't hop. "I want to jump into the water... Why can't I today?"

Mom put breakfast on the table. Fish, bread, and peas sat in a circle. She gently pushed the bread and peas off the plate. "Your plate looked like this yesterday, didn't it?" She pointed to the two empty spaces, then put the food back. "Empty spaces here mean less strength for you."

Beside her, her little brother held a shell and ate from another plate. A bite of fish, a bite of bread, a bite of peas. All the way around the plate! Pongi's little brother held up the empty plate and hopped. "Strong!"
"Let's play around-the-plate too." Mom sang, "Around the plate, yum, yum! Fish, yum! Bread, yum! Peas, yum!" Pongi took a little bite of bread. "Oh! It tastes lovely!"
Pongi picked up a pea and ate it too. "Sweet!" Then she ate the fish. Her plate was shiny and empty, with nothing left out. Pongi thumped her tail on the floor. "Around the plate, yum, yum!"
Pongi popped her head out of the water. Her legs felt light. Her little brother floated beside her. "My strength is back!" Pongi smiled a big smile.
It was evening. Pongi sang first. "Around the plate again today! One, look all around! Two, a bite of each! Three, don't leave anything out!" Fish, bread, peas, yum, yum, one after another.
Mom hugged Pongi tight. "Your plate is sparkling, Pongi!" Eating a bit of everything, without leaving anything out, fills you with strength. Pongi called, "Around the plate, yum, yum!"
